manual_overrides.zone_description: Single masonry corner building for labels 52, 54 and 02. The label notations remain provenance; no separate triangular or low corner building is generated.
manual_overrides.map_notes: `building-entrence-52-54-02` is one north-east corner footprint carrying the 52, 54 and 02 labels. User clarified this is one building. The numbers are interpreted as frontage/entrance labels on the same masonry corner building, not as separate masses. Do not split the visible model into a high bay and a low bay; keep one continuous footprint and one coherent roof. The georeferenced reread around N-50 shows a small rectangular rear open lightwell between this west/rear edge and parcel 50; add only one conservative upper window per floor looking into that void. User-supplied 2024 right-side street photos are used only as facade-material language for pale masonry, trim, and a restrained darker commercial base; they do not create extra street windows, doors, or separate buildings.

manual_overrides.zone_description: Merged south/east corner row containing the 41, 43, 45 and 16 building/entrance units. Four map labels indicate sub-units under a shared roof, not separate roof masses.
manual_overrides.map_notes: The `buildingentrence41-43-45-16` trace is not four separate freestanding footprints. On the Pervititch map it reads as one connected south/east corner row: four numbered building/entrance units (41, 43, 45, 16) combined under one common roof. Treat the numbers as sub-units in one shared-roof building. The final scene uses the full traced polygon as one merged building mass with one shared roof, multiple street doors, and subtle facade division seams rather than separate triangular/cut roof volumes. The west/left side of 41 is adjacent to the W-39 fountain/camli edge and must remain opaque: no awning, no shop band, no door/window glass on that side. Glass belongs only to the W-39-1 camli/vitre passage above/near the fountain.

manual_overrides.zone_description: Single connected Firin masonry mass. Internal number lines are frontage/entry divisions; no separate cut roof is generated.
manual_overrides.map_notes: `building-entrence-34-36-38` traces the Firin block on the north-west corner. The map text on this footprint reads Firin with VF/MB, 2 1/2, TR.4 and 3+ construction notes, so do not render it as a row of Mg./magazine storefronts. Model one connected masonry bakery mass with one coherent TR/tile roof, but keep the visible numbered entries 34, 36 and 38 as three distinct bakery/service entrances on the street frontage. The 34/Firin entry sits on the short diagonal/kinked west corner; 36 and 38 remain on the long west frontage. User-supplied 2024 street photos are used only as facade-material language here: pale plaster masonry and restrained bakery/service base, not copied modern signage or changed footprint geometry.

manual_overrides.map_labels: Camli, Vitre, church entrance, arched glazed fanlight
manual_overrides.zone_description: Lower blue-hatched Camli-Vitre church entrance passage. Photo correction: walls are normal plaster/masonry, not glass; the camli/vitre reading belongs to the top glass roof/light and to the arched fanlight/transom over the white church door.
manual_overrides.map_notes: The W-39/1 church-edge footprint must not be rendered as one all-glass block. The Pervititch crop shows Camli/Vitre only on the lower hatched passage; the user-supplied front photo confirms this is the Ayia Efimia church entrance: normal plastered low narthex walls, white double door, a glazed/iron arched fanlight above the door, and glass only at the top/roof zone. The Camli/Vitre roof/entry zone stops at the earlier vertical map break; the masonry/brick-narthex zone starts there so the glass-top area does not overlap brick/concrete massing. The adjacent yellow/wooden church-edge area labelled T. 1 bs. is not glass; it is a wooden one-storey-plus-basement annex with sheet-metal T roof. The church body face looking toward this wooden annex is interpreted as an internal/service side; those openings are interior doors, not exterior glass windows. The east/right area near the Clocher square remains an opaque side/narthex mass.
